decisions.decision: The hole, re-measured by the coordinator at 0433758 rather than taken from V2-083's escalation. (a) internal/api/api.go's domainError now ends in an unclassified branch that calls h.error(w, r, http.StatusInternalServerError, "internal_error", "internal server error") and deliberately never passes err.Error() (measured at api.go:1256-1261). The err value is dropped on the floor at that point: it is not returned, not stored, not written anywhere. (b) The panic-recovery branch at the top of the same file is the SAME hole and is older: ServeHTTP's deferred function reads `if recover() != nil` (api.go:49-53) and discards the recovered value without even binding it. (c) The reason neither text goes anywhere else is measured: ZERO non-test files under internal/ or cmd/ import "log" or "log/slog" -- the grep returns 0 files -- so this repository has no logging idiom at all. The only things that survive an unclassified failure today are the four response keys error/message/schema_version/correlation_id and the X-Correlation-ID header, and message is a constant. This task's whole content is to give (a) and (b) somewhere to be read, without giving the caller one extra byte.
decisions.rationale: V2-083's own evidence records this as its accepted cost and names V2-088 as the owner: 'this repository has no logging idiom at all ... so after this change the dependency's own text is visible NOWHERE in-process'. Including (b) is not scope creep but the same defect measured twice: a recovered panic is by definition an error nobody classified and nobody may show a caller, which is the exact class the outcome sentence names. Fixing only (a) would leave the repository able to lose a whole class of failure silently while claiming the class is now observable, and the panic branch is three lines away from the branch being changed in the same file.

decisions.decision: The record goes to STDOUT as one JSON object per line, and NOT to Firestore. Firestore is rejected for four measured reasons, the second of which is decisive. (1) The failure most worth recording IS a Firestore failure -- V2-079's reproduction was a gRPC InvalidArgument from internal/store/firestore's paged read -- so writing the record through the dependency that just failed loses the record exactly when it is needed. (2) A Firestore write consumes the daily write budget that internal/quota guards and that domainError's own first branch answers 429 for; a caller who can provoke a 500 could therefore drain the installation's write budget through the error path and take every mutation offline. That turns an observability feature into a denial-of-service amplifier and is a hard no. (3) It would require a new collection, a firestore.indexes.json entry, a retention rule, a contracts/ schema and a read surface -- four chain enrolments for a one-operator system. (4) Cloud Run captures a container's stdout into Cloud Logging with project-scoped IAM and platform-managed retention, and preview-local (owner's own machine, real process, Firestore emulator) runs the binary in the owner's own terminal, so stdout is already where the single operator is looking in BOTH deploy grades. The line carries "severity":"ERROR" so Cloud Logging's structured-logging convention gives it the right severity on stdout without depending on which stream it was written to.
decisions.rationale: The operating shape decides this. There is one operator, the management surface is owner-only but still authenticated, and the two grades are Cloud Run and preview-local. Both already have a durable, access-controlled, retention-managed, zero-new-code place for a process's stdout, and neither has any such place for an application-managed error collection. Reason (2) is the one that would still forbid Firestore even if the rest were free: the non_goals forbid a record the caller can grow without bound, and a caller-provokable write against a shared daily budget is worse than unbounded -- it is unbounded in the one resource whose exhaustion stops the product. Choosing 'both' inherits (1) and (2) for no additional information.

decisions.decision: The distinction between recording and responding, stated as the design's central rule. The RESPONSE for an unclassified error does not change by one byte: status 500, body exactly the four keys error="internal_error", message="internal server error", schema_version="v1", correlation_id, plus the X-Correlation-ID header. The RECORD carries all of that PLUS the request method, the request path and the error's own text. The text is recorded, and that is deliberate: the Firestore parent name V2-079 measured -- installation key, collection segments, byte offset -- is the operator's own infrastructure identifier, it is what makes the fault diagnosable, and the owner can already read it in the Firestore console and in the Terraform state. What was wrong before V2-083 was not that the text existed but that a CALLER received it. The audience is the whole difference, and it is enforced structurally rather than by care: the record is written to an io.Writer the Handler holds, never to the http.ResponseWriter, and the two code paths share no buffer.
decisions.rationale: This is the question a reviewer will ask first, and answering it with 'record less' would defeat the outcome: a record that omits the text leaves the operator exactly where V2-083 left them, holding a correlation id that resolves to nothing. Answering it with 'return the text' is non_goals item 1. The only remaining answer is that the text goes to a place the caller cannot reach, which is what a process's stdout under Cloud Run IAM is. Writing the rule down as an audience rule rather than a redaction rule also tells a future author what to do with a new field: ask who reads it, not how sensitive it looks.

decisions.decision: What may be recorded is a CLOSED Go struct with json tags and no map and no free-form field, so a call site cannot add anything: schema_version "v1", kind, severity "ERROR", observed_at, correlation_id, method, path, status, error, detail, detail_truncated, suppressed_before, and (only on the suppression marker) window_seconds and records_per_window. kind is one of exactly three values -- "unclassified_error" (domainError's unclassified branch), "recovered_panic" (ServeHTTP's recover branch) and "suppression_started" (d6's rate cap). What is NOT recorded is a list, and every entry is an absence the reader can check by reading one function signature: no request body, no response body, no header of any kind (so never the Authorization value), no query string (path only, RawQuery is not read at all), no caller identity beyond what the path itself contains, no stack trace, and no provider material.
decisions.rationale: V2-017 d12 settled this vocabulary for the provider seam -- record provider, version, executable path, session_id, usage, cost, durations, classification and the output DIGEST, and never the prompt, the Work Packet or the model's text -- and the same discipline transfers by making the record's shape a type rather than a convention. A closed struct is the difference between 'we agreed not to log the body' and 'there is no field a body could go in'. Excluding the query string rather than redacting it is the same move: a cursor is not a secret, but RawQuery is the one caller-controlled field with no length discipline of its own, and not reading it is cheaper to prove than sanitising it.

decisions.decision: Credential non-recording reuses the EXACT deny-list that already guards this repository's other diagnostic sink, with no second copy of any regular expression. internal/runner/secret_guard.go:44 exports RedactLog(value string) string, which applies the `secretValue` pattern (bearer <12+ chars> | -----BEGIN <...> PRIVATE KEY----- | gh[pousr]_<20+ chars>) and replaces every match with [REDACTED]; internal/runner/log.go's BoundedLog passes every write through it. internal/api may call it with no manifest consequence at all, because ci/components.json already declares api -> runner in dependencies (api deps measured: application, domain, infra, runner, web) and internal/api/api.go already imports the package. Both detail and path pass through RedactLog and are then capped. Prompts and raw provider responses are not redacted because they are structurally unreachable: internal/api holds no provider material, does not import internal/provider in any non-test file, and the recorder's input is a four-value tuple (correlation id, method, path, error).
decisions.rationale: The alternative -- internal/provider's exported ForbiddenPatternMatches and SecretPatternMatches -- was measured and rejected as a SOURCE dependency for one reason: api -> provider is declared only in verification_dependencies, so a non-test import would make internal/ci's VerifyDependencyCoverage demand an edit to ci/components.json, which is prohibited. Copying the pattern into internal/api instead was rejected because internal/provider's own comment says the exported predicates exist precisely so a scan asserts against the pattern the package applies 'rather than against a second copy of it that could drift'. Reusing runner.RedactLog satisfies both constraints at once: same deny-list, zero new edges, one owner. internal/provider is still used, but only from the test (d9), where the vdep already exists and is already derived by internal/api/live_dogfood_test.go.

decisions.decision: Bounded is a rate cap plus two size caps, and it is NOT sampling. Size: detail is capped at 256 bytes (the same cap internal/provider/provider.go:231-233 applies in safeMessage) and path at 256 bytes, each with detail_truncated recording the fact rather than hiding it, so one line is bounded by a constant of roughly 600 bytes. Rate: a fixed window of one minute with a cap of 32 records per window, evaluated lazily under a mutex on each attempt against the INJECTED clock -- no timer, no goroutine, no background sweeper. When the cap is first exceeded in a window the recorder emits exactly ONE line of kind "suppression_started" naming window_seconds and records_per_window and carrying no detail; every further attempt in that window writes nothing and increments a counter; the next line actually emitted carries suppressed_before with that exact count and resets it. Worst case per window is therefore 33 lines, and the fact that lines were dropped is visible twice -- immediately, as the marker, and exactly, as the count on the next line. Probabilistic sampling was rejected: it needs a source of randomness, which would make the recorder untestable by equality and would put a non-deterministic input into a package whose determinism rules forbid exactly that.
decisions.rationale: non_goals item 3 is the requirement and V2-083 measured why it bites: after the default flip, every route can answer 500, so a caller who can provoke one can provoke it in a loop. A cap with no visible drop is worse than no cap, because an operator reading 32 lines a minute cannot tell a steady trickle of one fault from a flood of a million. internal/runner/log.go is the precedent for the shape as well as the values: it caps by both bytes and lines and writes an explicit truncation marker exactly once, so the file always says that it was truncated. The marker-plus-count pair closes that precedent's tail gap, where a burst that ends the process would otherwise leave the drop count unreported.

decisions.decision: Time comes from an injected clock and from nowhere else. The recorder is built by an exported constructor, NewJSONOperatorRecorder(w io.Writer, clock application.Clock) (*JSONOperatorRecorder, error), which refuses a nil writer and a nil clock; observed_at and the window arithmetic both read that clock and the recorder never calls time.Now(). application.Clock (internal/application/ports.go:17, interface{ Now() time.Time }) is reused rather than declared again, because internal/api already imports internal/application. cmd/control-plane passes the productionClock{} it already constructs (cmd/control-plane/main.go:24-26, :176); internal/api's tests pass the existing steppable framingClock (internal/api/api_test.go:3138, nextDay). api.Config gains exactly ONE new field, OperatorRecorder, whose nil value means 'record nothing', so no existing test's behaviour and no existing test's output changes.
decisions.rationale: A logger that reads the wall clock is the classic way determinism dies, and it would make the emitted line unassertable by equality -- which is the only assertion strong enough to prove a closed field set. Putting the clock in the CONSTRUCTOR rather than in api.Config keeps api.go itself clock-free for this feature and makes 'the recorder does not read time' checkable as a source property, which d10 turns into a test. Defaulting the Config field to nil is what protects V2-083's 202-row pin table and its 25-route x 2-variant fault test from suddenly printing 50 lines they never printed before; the existing fixture opts in explicitly instead.

decisions.decision: The record is written from internal/api, not from internal/application, and the layering is the reason rather than convenience. Only domainError knows that an error was unclassified -- that judgement IS the api layer's classification, measured at api.go:1204-1261 -- and only ServeHTTP knows a panic was recovered. The correlation id that makes the record joinable to what the caller saw lives in the request context and is put there by api.ServeHTTP (api.go:54-59, CorrelationID at :64-67). internal/application cannot participate without learning HTTP status codes, which would invert the dependency this repository maintains. Import edges: internal/api gains "io" (already imported), "sync", "encoding/json" (already imported), "time" (already imported), application.Clock (already imported) and runner.RedactLog (already imported); cmd/control-plane already imports internal/api and internal/application. Net change to the component graph is ZERO in both dependencies and verification_dependencies. The only test-side import that is new to internal/api is internal/provider, and api -> provider is ALREADY declared in verification_dependencies and already derived from internal/api/live_dogfood_test.go, so nothing moves there either.
decisions.rationale: The task explicitly asks whether a new edge is needed, and the honest answer is measured: no. That matters operationally, not just aesthetically, because ci/components.json, Makefile, go.mod, go.sum and devbox.* are all prohibited, so internal/ci's manifest and dependency-coverage checks become a STOPPING CONDITION rather than a chore -- if either goes red, the implementation reached for a package this design did not authorise, and the correct response is to escalate rather than to edit the manifest.

decisions.decision: No new HTTP route, and no owner-facing read surface of any kind. GET /v1/... is rejected because it costs four things this task has no business paying: an entry in contracts/openapi/openapi-v1.yaml, which moves the contracts component key and the release BundleDigest and enrols this task in the api-contract chain; a durable store to read from, which d2 already refused; paging and therefore a cursor, which is V2-079's boundary; and a role/authorisation judgement about who may read failures. It also costs the one thing that must not be paid: a read surface makes the recorded text reachable over HTTP again, which is precisely the disclosure V2-083 closed, and no authorisation rule makes that a good trade for one operator. What IS delivered instead is a documented way to read the records: a section appended to docs/operations/gcp-runbook.md giving the Cloud Logging filter for Cloud Run and the plain 'it is on the process's stdout' answer for preview-local, plus the field list and the explicit statement of what a record never contains.
decisions.rationale: The runbook was measured and says nothing about logs at all -- grep for 'log' and 'Cloud Logging' over docs/operations/gcp-runbook.md returns nothing -- so without the documentation half, 'somewhere to read' is true of the system and false of the operator, and the outcome would be only half delivered. A markdown section is the cheapest possible read surface: component-docs is `! rg -n 'TODO(ci)' docs README.md`, it enters no chain, and it can be deleted in a revert with no consequence. Recording the preview-local caveat there is also honest: measured, internal/api/live_local_test.go starts the binary through runner.ProcessSupervisor with Stdout nil (live_local_test.go:159), so the child inherits the test process's stdout and the records appear in `go test -v` output -- visible to a human, but not assertable in that test, which is prohibited from being edited.

decisions.decision: What is measured, and in what order. (1) Baseline: run the existing internal/api suite green on the UNEDITED tree and record the top-level test list, so the after-count is provably the before-count plus exactly the tests this task adds. (2) Add internal/api/operator_record.go and internal/api/operator_record_test.go and prove the recorder ALONE, with no HTTP involved: a bytes.Buffer sink and the steppable clock, asserting the emitted line by equality; the closed key set by unmarshalling into map[string]any and comparing the key set exactly, the same technique V2-083 used for the four response keys; redaction and 256-byte truncation with detail_truncated true; the 33-line worst case per window with the suppression marker and the exact suppressed_before count on the next line after the clock is stepped past the window; and a nil writer or nil clock refused by the constructor. (3) Only then wire domainError's unclassified branch and ServeHTTP's recover branch, and add api.Config.OperatorRecorder. (4) Prove the seam over HTTP by reusing V2-083's own fixtures unchanged: for all 25 faultRoutes in both variants, exactly one record whose correlation_id equals the response body's correlation_id AND the X-Correlation-ID header; and for at least one row per distinct classified status the pin table already produces, ZERO records. (5) Re-run V2-083's two tests and assert both are byte-unchanged and green.
decisions.rationale: Proving the recorder before wiring it is what makes the field-set and bounding claims measurements rather than hopes, and it keeps the hard assertions out of the HTTP tests where 202 pin rows and 50 fault cases are already carrying V2-083's guarantee. Step (4)'s negative half is the one that keeps d3's rule true over time: without 'zero records for a classified error' the recorder drifts into logging every 404, which floods the operator's view with caller mistakes and makes the 500s -- the only records that carry information nobody else has -- impossible to find. Reusing faultRoutes rather than writing a new route list means the record's coverage is the SAME 25 routes V2-083 proved, by construction, and cannot fall behind it.

decisions.decision: V2-083's guarantees are inherited as stopping conditions, not as things to re-derive. TestEveryRouteStillAnswersTheStatusItAnsweredBefore (internal/api/api_test.go:4092, measured 202 rows in pinRows() at :3807-4091) must stay byte-unchanged in both the table and the assertions and stay green, including its PINBODY byte-comparison logging. TestAStorageFaultIsNotReportedAsTheCallersMistake (:4327, 25 faultRoutes x 2 variants) must keep every assertion byte-unchanged and keep passing, in particular the injectedStoreFaultFragments absence check (:4156-4166) -- eight fragments including the installation key install-7f3a and the doubled projects/agentic-loop-local parent name. TestTheBacklogStillRefusesACursorItDidNotIssue (:2950) must stay byte-unchanged. The ONLY edit permitted inside newFaultFixture (:4213) is additive: a recorder field on faultFixture and the corresponding api.Config field, three lines, touching no assertion and no route row. If any of these needs a real edit, the design was departed from: stop and escalate.
decisions.rationale: This task exists because of V2-083 and the fastest way to make it a net loss is to weaken what V2-083 bought. The absence-of-text assertion is the one at genuine risk here, because this task's whole purpose is to move that text somewhere -- and 'somewhere' is one wrong argument away from being the ResponseWriter. Keeping those assertions byte-unchanged while adding a record next to them is exactly the measurement that the text went to the operator and not to the caller. Editing newFaultFixture rather than duplicating its seeding is the smaller risk of the two: the seeding is 40 lines of real state through real routes, and a second copy would drift.

decisions.decision: Production wiring is part of this task, in cmd/control-plane/main.go, and it is the only reason cmd/** is in allowed_paths. run() builds the recorder with NewJSONOperatorRecorder(os.Stdout, productionClock{}) -- the clock value it already constructs at main.go:176 -- returns its error the way it returns every other constructor's error, and passes it in the api.Config literal at main.go:183. Without this the outcome is false in both deploy grades: a nil Config field records nothing, so the feature would exist only in tests. Two production behaviours are asserted to be unmoved: `go run ./cmd/control-plane --version` still prints exactly the version and nothing else, because the --version branch returns before run() (main.go:96-100) and `make smoke` greps that stdout with an anchored regex; and no record is written during startup or shutdown, because the only two call sites are inside a request.
decisions.rationale: The measured alternative -- defaulting the sink to os.Stdout inside internal/api when the Config field is nil -- was rejected for a concrete reason, not a stylistic one: every existing test that calls api.New would start writing records, which means 202 pin rows and 50 fault cases would print lines into `go test` output that they have never printed, and any future assertion on test output becomes noise-dependent. Explicit wiring keeps 'off unless asked' as the default and puts the decision where the process's other environment decisions already are. Checking `make smoke` is not paranoia: it is the one existing check that asserts a byte-exact stdout from this binary, and a stdout-based recorder is exactly the change that could break it.

decisions.decision: Rollback is a plain revert with no data or client consequence, and this is a property rather than a hope. Reverting means deleting internal/api/operator_record.go and internal/api/operator_record_test.go, undoing one branch in domainError, one branch in ServeHTTP, one field in api.Config, three lines in newFaultFixture, one constructor call and one struct field in cmd/control-plane/main.go, and one markdown section. Nothing else has to be undone, because this change writes no document, reads no document, alters no stored field, adds no route, adds no request or response field, changes no error's Error() text, changes no status code and touches no contract. Records already emitted are inert: they live in Cloud Logging or in a terminal, they carry their own schema_version, and no code in this repository reads them, so there is no state only the new code can interpret.
decisions.rationale: The honest way to state a rollback story is to enumerate what could survive the revert and show that each item is inert. The one candidate for a lingering effect is the emitted lines themselves, and they are the reason schema_version is in the record: a future reader that DOES parse them can tell which shape it is holding, and until such a reader exists there is nothing to migrate.

decisions.decision: Chain position, stated for the coordinator. Components: api, control-plane, docs. Measured conflicts among the open tasks: V2-087 (queued) holds internal/api/api_test.go; V2-085 (blocked on V2-087) has no Work Order yet; V2-086 (blocked on V2-085) holds internal/api/api.go AND cmd/control-plane/main.go, which is a direct two-file conflict; V2-084 (blocked on V2-086) holds internal/api/api.go and internal/api/api_test.go; V2-080 (blocked) depends on V2-087 and V2-088 and is the live re-observation that must follow. Therefore serialize this task AFTER V2-087 and BEFORE V2-085, V2-086 and V2-084, and before V2-080. contracts/**, internal/domain/**, internal/application/**, internal/store/**, internal/quota/**, internal/provider/** (source), firestore.indexes.json and infra/** are prohibited BY DESIGN, each for a reason written into an acceptance item, not by omission.
decisions.rationale: Three open tasks want internal/api/api_test.go and two want cmd/control-plane/main.go, so ordering is the only question, and the window between V2-087 and V2-085 is the only place this task fits without a rebase: V2-086 takes both of this task's source files, and everything after V2-086 inherits that. Going after V2-087 rather than before it is deliberate too -- V2-087 changes what the memory adapter charges for a reservation, which is exactly the change V2-083's 429 pin row exists to catch, and letting that land first means this task measures its pin-table baseline against a table that is already settled.

verification: devbox run --pure -e AGENTIC_LOOP_LIVE_LOCAL=1 -- scripts/firestore-emulator.sh go test -count=1 -v -run TestControlPlanePreviewLocalLive ./internal/api
risks: The single largest risk is that the recorded text reaches the caller after all -- a stray h.error(w, r, ..., detail) while wiring, or a recorder handed the http.ResponseWriter. V2-083's injectedStoreFaultFragments absence check over all 25 routes in both variants is the guard and must stay byte-unchanged; if it goes red the task has recreated the exact defect it was created to compensate for, and the answer is to stop, not to adjust the fragment list.

The bounding can be wired in the wrong place. A cap applied per-Handler-instance or per-request rather than inside the single recorder value gives a caller an unbounded record again, and a cap applied to the Handler's own field would be reset by any code path that rebuilds it. All of the window state, the mutex and both size caps live inside JSONOperatorRecorder, which cmd/control-plane constructs exactly once.

The clock is easy to leak back in. A single time.Now() inside the recorder -- for observed_at, for the window, or in a fallback when the clock is nil -- makes the emitted line unassertable by equality and quietly voids the determinism rule for the whole package. The constructor refuses a nil clock and a source-level assertion checks that the new file contains no time.Now call.

Secret-shaped fixture strings are a trap in two directions: a literal bearer token, PEM header or gh token written into internal/api/operator_record_test.go can trip gitleaks through `make secrets` even though it is a fixture, while a fixture that is too weak proves nothing about redaction. Build every secret-shaped fixture by concatenating a prefix with a suffix -- the same trick already mandated for module-path literals -- so the pattern exists at run time and not in the file, and run `make secrets` to confirm it.

cmd/control-plane/main.go and internal/api/api.go are both held by V2-086, and internal/api/api_test.go is held by V2-087 and V2-084. Running any of those concurrently with this task conflicts in a file. The window between V2-087 and V2-085 is the only conflict-free position and the coordinator must hold it.

make smoke asserts a byte-exact stdout from cmd/control-plane --version with an anchored regex. A recorder that writes anything during startup, or a debug line left in main.go, turns that check red for a reason that looks unrelated to this task.

Recording every error rather than only unclassified ones is the failure mode that makes the feature useless without failing any obvious test: a flood of 400s and 404s buries the 500s, which are the only records carrying information the caller does not already have. The negative half of the HTTP measurement -- zero records for every classified status -- is not optional.
